Request a written determination or a pre-application meeting to confirm the pathway before filing ABC or health applications.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms continuation of use, file the ABC Type 41 original application online through ABC's online portal, including the signed lease, entity documents, seller's permit, and the Planning Department's written confirmation that the restaurant use is established. What to say: In the ABC application, describe the premises as a bona fide eating place with a full commercial kitchen, table seating, and meals served during all hours of alcohol service. Attach Planning's written confirmation that the restaurant use is legally established and authorized to continue in the CCB district per Planning Code Section 810. Submit the signed lease, California Secretary of State entity registration, seller's permit, and photos of the interior showing kitchen and dining areas. ABC will route the application to SFPD and Planning for 30-day referral review, then post a notice at the premises for 30 days. Budget 60–120 days if unprotested; add one to three months if the census tract's undue concentration triggers a Public Convenience or Necessity finding request from the city.
outcomes.note: Records don't specify online filing, the detailed description requirements, Section 810, or routing to SFPD and Planning for 30-day referral review.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File for or renew the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and the Health Permit to Operate through the SF Department of Public Health online portal, confirming continuation of the existing restaurant use. What to say: State that the restaurant use at 667 Commercial St continues as previously approved by Planning in 1998 and 2014, and that beer and wine service is being added under an ABC Type 41 application. DPH will route the health permit application to Planning for a zoning referral; Planning should approve it administratively as continuation of use if step 1 confirmed that pathway. Attach the ABC application receipt, the certified food safety manager certificate, and proof of workers' compensation insurance. The health permit referral typically takes 14–45 days for administrative approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA (free, online, often same-day) and register for California EDD payroll taxes if not already done, as both are prerequisites for the ABC license. What to say: Register online through the CDTFA portal for the seller's permit (no fee) and the EDD e-Services for Business portal for employer registration (no fee). ABC will not issue the Type 41 license until the seller's permit number is on file. If you already hold these registrations, provide the account numbers on the ABC application.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Enroll all alcohol-serving staff and managers in ABC-approved Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training within 60 days of hire, and post the certification list on site for ABC inspections. What to say: Register each employee on the ABC RBS Portal ($3 per person), complete an approved RBS course (about $10–$25 per person), and pass the exam. Download the certificates and keep a current list of certified staff on the premises. ABC inspectors will ask for this list during routine inspections and at the time of license issuance.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 60 to 210 days. Estimated government cost: $1,470 to $2,600. Notes: Timeline of 60–210 days and cost of $1,470–$2,600 are for approvals when granted, covering the Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and the Health Permit to Operate. ABC Type 41 application: 60–120 days per the permit catalog if unprotested; one to three months longer if census tract 611.01's undue concentration requires a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city. Health permit to operate: 14–45 days per the catalog entry. The timeline assumes Planning confirms continuation of use; if Planning requires a new Conditional Use Authorization, add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 per catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization, based on the one CUA comparable at 838 Grant Ave that took 183 days from filing to approval. Government fees: ABC Type 41 application $1,000–$1,600, health permit to operate $470–$1,000 (2026–27 schedule). Not included: San Francisco Business Registration Certificate $55–$700 (prerequisite, typically $55–$95 for a small restaurant), California Seller's Permit (free), EDD employer registration (free), RBS training $13–$55 per employee, ASCAP and BMI music licenses $600–$5,000 combined (not government fees), and any building permit if a change of occupancy is determined. The pending Miscellaneous Permit 2022-011138MIS filed November 14, 2022 at this address may affect the timeline; verify its status with Planning before filing.
